nodes.name: Weekly Schedule
nodes.notes: Starts the workflow on a timer — weekly. No input data; downstream nodes fetch what they need.

nodes.name: Keep Valid Emails
nodes.notes: Drops items that fail the condition; only qualifying items continue (no false branch).

nodes.name: Segment Audience
nodes.notes: Two-way gate on ={{ ($json.score ?? 50) >= 50 }}. TRUE continues the happy path, FALSE takes the alternate branch. Watch out: The false branch carries the non-matching items — wire it deliberately rather than leaving it dangling.

nodes.name: Step 1 — Welcome (Gmail)
nodes.notes: Sends an email via Gmail — subject is the first line of the message body, recipient comes from the item's email field. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Google OAuth2. Google Cloud Console → enable Gmail API → OAuth consent screen → OAuth client ID (Web).

nodes.name: Tag for Slow Nurture
nodes.notes: Upserts a row into 'Email Tracker', matched on messageId — re-running with the same key updates the row instead of duplicating it. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Google OAuth2 / service account. Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.

nodes.name: Wait Before Step 2
nodes.notes: Pauses 2 days — spacing calls to respect rate limits. Watch out: Long waits survive restarts, but the resume URL is single-use.

nodes.name: Converted Already?
nodes.notes: Two-way gate on ={{ $json.status }}. TRUE continues the happy path, FALSE takes the alternate branch. Watch out: The false branch carries the non-matching items — wire it deliberately rather than leaving it dangling.

# Onboard leads: Gmail

**Pattern:** Drip Sequence · **Level:** Expert · **Trigger:** Scheduled

## Overview

Runs on a schedule, and covers inbox-triage work end to end across Gmail, Google Sheets, Notion and Google Drive.

It moves through 28 working steps plus a 3-node error rail, in this order:

1. Weekly Schedule
2. Keep Valid Emails
3. Segment Audience
4. Step 1 — Welcome (Gmail)
5. Tag for Slow Nurture
6. Wait Before Step 2
7. Converted Already?
8. Step 2 — Value Nudge (Gmail)
9. Mark Converted — Stop Drip
10. Update Drip Status
11. Load Previous Snapshot
12. Compute Drift vs Snapshot
13. Enrich with Reference Data
14. Fold In Enrichment Fields
15. Serialize Run Output (CSV)
16. Archive Copy to Google Drive
17. Stamp Completion Time
18. Persist Run Metadata
19. Fingerprint for Idempotency
20. Drop Already-Processed Items
21. Offload to Post-Process Sub-workflow
22. Record Sub-workflow Result
23. Stamp Processing Time
24. Save Execution Metadata
25. Tag Pipeline Metadata
26. Summarize Run Stats
27. Append Audit Row (Google Sheets)
28. Send Summary to Gmail

Anything that throws leaves the happy path at that node and goes down the red rail — Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Gmail → Park in Dead-Letter Queue — so a failure is reported rather than silently lost.

## Why it exists

Doing inbox-triage work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

Weekly Schedule → Keep Valid Emails → Segment Audience → Step 1 — Welcome (Gmail) → Tag for Slow Nurture → Wait Before Step 2 → Converted Already? → Step 2 — Value Nudge (Gmail) → Mark Converted — Stop Drip → Update Drip Status → Load Previous Snapshot → Compute Drift vs Snapshot → Enrich with Reference Data → Fold In Enrichment Fields → Serialize Run Output (CSV) → Archive Copy to Google Drive → Stamp Completion Time → Persist Run Metadata → Fingerprint for Idempotency → Drop Already-Processed Items → Offload to Post-Process Sub-workflow → Record Sub-workflow Result → Stamp Processing Time → Save Execution Metadata → Tag Pipeline Metadata → Summarize Run Stats → Append Audit Row (Google Sheets) → Send Summary to Gmail → Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Gmail → Park in Dead-Letter Queue

## Use it for

- Teams keeping Gmail and Google Sheets aligned by hand for inbox triage
- Inbox triage sequences that run over days and must survive a restart before Gmail
- Inbox triage work where "Keep Valid Emails" is still a manual step before Gmail
- Inbox triage work that only reaches Gmail on a schedule, when someone remembers to start it

## You get

- Keeps Gmail and Google Sheets in step for inbox triage, without anyone re-typing a row
- Safe to re-run: records already in Gmail or Google Sheets are skipped, across all 31 nodes of this inbox-triage build
- A failed Gmail or Google Sheets call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 31 nodes in this inbox-triage build
- The pause before Gmail is durable — a inbox-triage run survives a restart
- Every inbox-triage run leaves an audit row behind, alongside Gmail

## Before first run
Connect credentials: API key / bearer for the target API; Google OAuth2; Google OAuth2 / service account; Notion integration token.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

Every step checks 'Converted Already?' before sending — a drip campaign that keeps emailing someone who already bought is the fastest way to burn trust. The Wait node's durable resume state (via `webhookId`) is what lets a multi-day wait survive an n8n restart instead of being held only in memory.

## Practice exercises

About as deep as this pattern goes — extend it:

1. Add a 4th drip step with its own wait/exit-check pair.
2. Manually flip a test record's status to 'converted' mid-drip and confirm the ladder stops sending.
3. Shorten the wait durations so the full ladder runs in minutes instead of days, for testing.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**Google OAuth2**
Google Cloud Console → enable Gmail API → OAuth consent screen → OAuth client ID (Web).
_Gotcha:_ Add n8n's OAuth redirect URL exactly as shown in the credential, or the consent loop fails.

**Google OAuth2 / service account**
Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.
_Gotcha:_ Using a Service Account? Share the spreadsheet with its email address or it 404s.

**Notion integration token**
notion.so/my-integrations → New integration → copy the Internal Integration Token.
_Gotcha:_ Then open the database → ••• → Connections → add your integration, or every call 404s.

**API key / bearer for the target API**
Whatever the target API issues — usually a bearer token or API key.
_Gotcha:_ Store it as a credential, never typed into the node's parameters.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

**HTTP node returns 401 or 403**
Cause: Wrong or unscoped credential, or the API expects a header this request isn't sending.
Fix: Verify the key directly with curl first, then confirm the auth type matches what the API documents.

**HTTP node returns 429**
Cause: Rate limited by the provider.
Fix: Raise the wait between calls or lower the batch size. Retries already back off, but they cannot beat a hard quota.

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 Error handling & retries

External calls retry **3× with 2s backoff**. Anything still failing exits through its node's error output into the red error rail → context is captured and the on-call channel is alerted. Failures are also parked in a dead-letter queue for replay. Set an n8n **Error Workflow** in settings as the final safety net.

## ⏱ Rate limiting

Work is batched and spaced with Wait so provider quotas aren't tripped. If you hit 429s, lower the batch size or raise the wait — throughput drops, reliability rises.

## 🧹 Data quality

Dedupe/diff steps make re-runs safe: the same input twice will not create duplicate records. If you change the key fields, clear n8n's dedupe memory (node → 'Clear stored keys') before the next run.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your inbox triage process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- Gmail: request the narrowest send/read scope the nodes need — full mailbox access is rarely required.
- Google Sheets: share the single spreadsheet with the service account rather than granting drive-wide access.
- Notion: share only the target database with the integration. An integration sees nothing you have not explicitly shared.
- Google Drive: scope the credential to the one folder this workflow writes to, not `drive.readonly` across the account.

The HTTP node sends a secret: keep it in a header credential, never in the URL — query strings land in proxy and execution logs.

**Do not log**
inbox-triage payloads carry personal data (names, email addresses, phone numbers). Log the record id and the outcome, not the record. n8n retains full execution data by default — turn that down for this workflow in Settings → Executions if these runs touch real contacts.
